text:
amy_chen: kicking off thread for Aurora enterprise commit POC — need capacity + preheat/autoscale clarification from infra before i send final answers to the customer. short bullets below.

diego_roberts: quick baseline: target steady 30 rps (1800 req/min) with short bursts up to 300 rps for ~60-120s. avg prompt+response ~400 tokens, max 1024.

ev an_miller: typo: i'll assume 30 rps avg with concurrency ~40. for model M-XL (quantized) we measure ~12k tokens/s per A100-equivalent under our runtime, so estimated reserved GPUs = ceil((30 * 400) / (12_000)) -> ~1. But bursts push that.

linda_ng: so is 1 reserved sufficient? sales needs a conservative commit number for billing. they expect an SLA buffer.

diego_roberts: recommend reserved=3 for commit (hedged to 3x steady) with autoscale headroom for bursts via burst credits. that gets p95 latency headroom and avoids queueing on preheat.

amy_chen: can you show the autoscale policy snippet i can paste in the proposal? include preheat + KV warmup note.

diego_roberts: paste below — feel free to redact internal names: 
```
autoscale_policy:
  reserved_gpus: 3            # commit capacity (monthly pricing)
  min_gpus: 0                 # start cold when idle
  burst_credit_pool: 1500     # token-based burst credit to cover spikes
  scale_up_threshold: p95_latency_ms > 300
  scale_down_threshold: p95_latency_ms < 200 for 5m
  preheat_kv_warm: true       # prewarm session KV cache on commit start
```

ev an_miller: note on KV warm: recommend running a KV-warm job at preheat to seed top-25% user prefixes — saves ~40% p95 during first 2 mins of surge. i can attach a small script.

linda_ng: pricing question from sales: if we reserve 3 GPUs, what does monthly expected spend look like vs reserve 1 + burst? need 3-line comparison for the deck.

diego_roberts: ballpark: reserve1 + burst = lower commit fee but ~30% higher variable token/GPU-hours due to cold spill. reserve3 = higher committed fee but ~15-20% lower variable cost and more predictable latency. i will send numbers after evan runs sim.

ev an_miller: running quick sim now — sim profile: 30 rps steady, 300 rps spikes 2x/day length 90s, seq dist 80% 256-512, 20% 512-1024. link: https://internal.redwood/sim/aurora/1768012345 (run queued).

amy_chen: also need security questionnaire item: they asked whether preheat uses customer data and how KV seed jobs access session prefixes. ops needs an answer for the security sheet.

diego_roberts: preheat KV job uses synthetic prefixes generated from anonymized prompt templates; we do not upload customer PII. access controlled by VPC links for Private, and for Dedicated we can run preheat within customer's VPC. add that to questionnaire.

linda_ng: can someone paste one-liner for security answer so i can drop in the questionnaire?

ev an_miller: one-liner: "KV preheat jobs use anonymized synthetic prefixes and run within the customer's network boundary for Dedicated/Private deployments; no customer PII is uploaded to Redwood-managed preheat jobs."

amy_chen: perfect. last: ops blocker — on the Dedicated side, they want AZ affinity and eviction tolerance. can we guarantee AZ spread for the reserved pool?

diego_roberts: yes — we can pin reserved pool across 2 AZs for resilience. eviction tolerance: reserve3 gives us headroom to survive single-AZ interruption for this workload for short windows, otherwise autoscale to other regions as fallback. include this in the runbook.

opsbot: Deploy-bot: preheat job template created -> job id j-aurora-2345, scheduled when commit is accepted. :white_check_mark:

amy_chen: thanks everyone — action items: (1) evan attach sim results + cost delta (2) diego paste conservative monthly estimates (3) linda drop security one-liner into questionnaire and confirm. i'll sync with sales in 24h. :thumbsup:
